options.why: Draws the two equal sloping sides sloping towards each other instead of parallel, which turns the end face into a trapezium.
This is the side view of the prism, which is a plain rectangle, not the view from the front.
This is the top view: the line is the edge where the sloping face meets the flat top face.

questions.solution_text:
The front view is the end face of the prism.
That face has two pairs of parallel, equal sides, so it is a parallelogram, which is shape $2$.

options.text: a rectangle with a line across it

options.why: Misses the edge where the two faces on that side of the prism meet, which runs the whole length of the solid.
Gives the cross-section of the prism, which is the front view, instead of the view from the side.

options.text: a rectangle with two lines down it
options.why: This is the top view; the two lines are the edges where the flat top meets each sloping face.

questions.solution_text:
From the side the outline is a rectangle as wide as the prism is long and as tall as the prism is high.
On that side of the prism two faces meet along an edge halfway up, and that edge runs the whole length of the solid, so one line is drawn across the rectangle.

options.why: Draws a single ridge line as for a triangular prism, but this prism has a flat top with an edge on each side of it.
Ignores the two edges where the flat top face meets the sloping faces, which do show from above.
Gives the cross-section of the prism, which is the front view, instead of the view from above.

questions.solution_text:
From above the outline is a rectangle as wide as the widest part of the prism and as long as the prism.
The flat top face meets a sloping face on each side, so two lines are drawn inside the outline, which is shape $3$.

options.text: It is the mirror image of the front view.
It is exactly the same as the front view.
options.why: Assumes the two end faces always look the same, which only happens when the cross-section is symmetrical.

options.text: It is the front view turned upside down.
options.why: Turns the view through $180^{\circ}$ instead of reflecting it left to right, so the flat base would end up on top.
Gives the side view of the prism rather than the view from the back, which still shows the cross-section.

questions.solution_text:
The back view shows the end face at the far end of the prism, but you look at it from the opposite direction.
So everything on the right of the front view appears on the left, and the back view is the mirror image of the front view.

options.text: a rectangle with a line across it

options.why: Gives the front view, which shows the step, instead of the view from the side.
Misses the line at the height where the shorter prism ends and the surface drops.

options.text: a rectangle with a line down the middle
options.why: Draws the line running the wrong way: in the side view the step runs across the solid, not down it.

questions.solution_text:
From the side the outline is a rectangle as wide as the solid is long and as tall as the taller prism.
The top of the shorter prism runs the whole length of the solid at a lower height, so one line is drawn across the rectangle.

options.why: Draws one line as for a single step, but four prisms of different heights give three places where the surface drops.
Gives the front view, which shows the steps themselves, instead of the outline seen from above.
Treats the solid as one rectangular prism and misses every edge where the height changes.

questions.solution_text:
From above the outline is one rectangle covering all four prisms.
The four prisms have four different heights, so the surface drops at three places and three lines are drawn inside the outline, which is shape $1$.

options.why: Uses the rectangular side outline as the front face and misses the triangular front view and top ridge.
Adds vertical walls below the sloping roof, giving a five-sided front view and an extra horizontal edge in the side view.
Replaces the triangular peak with a flat top, giving a trapezium front view and two lines in the top view.

questions.solution_text:
Use the triangular front view as the end face and extend it along the prism's length.
Sketch $1$ has the triangular front view, the plain rectangular side view and the single ridge shown in the top view.

options.why: Omits the middle height, so the front has only one step and the top has only one internal line.
Reflects the front left to right, placing the tallest section on the right and reversing which side has visible step edges.
Ignores the changes in height and uses the plain left-side rectangle as the solid's front face.

questions.solution_text:
Extend the three-step front face along the length shown in the side and top views.
The tallest section is on the left of the front view. It hides the lower sections from the left side, while both step edges are visible from the right side.
Sketch $1$ matches these views and has the two joining edges shown in the top view.
